questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"In many Tunisian homes, grandparents live with their grandchildren. They tell old stories, help with homework and look after the little ones. In return, the children learn patience and respect, and the old people never feel alone."

What is the main idea of this passage?

options.text: Grandparents tell old stories and look after the little ones.
Old people are too tired to live with young children.
Living together helps grandparents and grandchildren.
Children learn their lessons better with their parents.

questions.explanation: The gist is the idea every sentence supports: the grandparents give stories, help and care, and the children give back patience, respect and company — so living together helps both. "Grandparents tell old stories and look after the little ones" is true, but it is only a detail of the second sentence. Tiredness and parents are never mentioned.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"The school canteen serves lunch from Monday to Friday, between 12:00 and 2:00. On Saturday it serves only breakfast, and on Sunday it stays closed."

On which day does the canteen serve breakfast only?
questions.explanation: Scan for the key word "breakfast": it appears in one sentence only — "On Saturday it serves only breakfast". Sunday is tempting because it is also different from the other days, but on Sunday the canteen is closed. Wednesday and Friday follow the lunch timetable.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"The teacher gave back the tests. Lina read her mark twice. Then she smiled, put the paper carefully in her bag and ran out to call her mother."

What can we infer about Lina?

options.text: She got a good mark and felt proud.
She did not understand her mark.
She lost her test paper on the way.
She got a bad mark and was angry with her teacher.

questions.explanation: The text never gives the mark, but the clues prove it: she smiles, keeps the paper carefully and runs to call her mother — the reaction of a proud pupil. "She got a bad mark and was angry with her teacher" goes against every clue: an angry pupil does not smile. Nothing suggests confusion or a lost paper.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"Volunteers planted two hundred young trees along the river last spring. Today they are tall and green, and families come to sit in their shade."

In the second sentence, what does "they" refer to?
questions.explanation: "They" is plural; put the noun back and test it: "the trees are tall and green" and give shade. "The volunteers" is the tempting answer because it is the first plural noun of the text, but people are not "green" and do not give shade. The river is singular.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"Buses in our town are very convenient: the stops are close to every school, a bus comes every ten minutes, and a ticket costs only one dinar."

What does the word "convenient" most probably mean here?
questions.explanation: The words after the colon explain "convenient": near the schools, frequent, cheap — so the buses are practical and easy to use. "Modern but quite expensive" is contradicted by "only one dinar", and "far and hard to reach" by "close to every school". Noise is never mentioned.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"Plastic bags are cheap and light, whereas cloth bags last for years and do not pollute the sea."

What is the function of the linker "whereas" in this sentence?

options.text: It gives the cause of the pollution.
It introduces a result of the first idea.
It adds a second, similar advantage.

questions.explanation: "Whereas" is a contrast linker: it opposes plastic bags (cheap, light) to cloth bags (lasting, clean). It does not add a similar idea — the text compares the two kinds of bags, it does not add them. A cause needs "because", and a result "so" or "as a result".

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"Saying "please" and "thank you" costs nothing, but these small words can change a lot: they can turn a stranger into a friend and an argument into a calm talk."

What is the writer's main message?

options.text: Polite words are expensive and difficult to learn.
Small polite words have a big effect on people.
People should never talk to strangers.

questions.explanation: The whole passage opposes the small cost of polite words ("costs nothing") to their big effect (a friend instead of a stranger, calm instead of an argument): small polite words have a big effect. "Polite words are expensive and difficult to learn" contradicts "costs nothing". The text never says strangers are dangerous.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"The summer festival of our town offers something for everyone: films in the open air, live music until midnight and games for young children."

Which detail is mentioned in the passage?

options.text: a football match on the beach

questions.explanation: Scanning the list after the colon gives three activities: open-air films, live music until midnight and games for children. Only "live music until midnight" appears in the text. A cooking competition, a football match and an art exhibition are festival activities you may imagine, but the text does not mention them.
